full_judgment: 4.5 As stated above, a transfer of immovable property passes forthwith all the title, interest in the transferor in favour of the transferee as per the provisions of Section 8 of the Transfer of Property Act. Now, the requirement of registration of such transfer deed is requirement of law in order to safeguard such transfer from any future question, and by such registration, the State becomes party to such transfer, and the Legislature has given a kind of protection in favour of such registered transfer by operation of law in that it gets presumption of correctness once it is registered, unless contrary is proved. Section 47 of the Registration Act is very much clear in this regard which provides that a registered document shall operate from the time which it would have commenced to operate, if no registration thereof had been required or made and not from the time of its registration. Therefore, the Legislature has made it clear that since the registration of a transfer deed is a formal requirement, the transfer in fact started to operate at the time when such transfer is made by way of execution of transfer deeds although, at that point of time, the said deed was not registered formally. Now, the Legislature has subsequently made such transfer mandatory even by saying that any transfer without such registration will be void. This statutory requirement of registration of transfer deed in respect of immovable property has been provided only to safeguard the transferor and the transferee from any manipulation or subsequent fraudulent act in respect of such transfer, as because the State becomes witness to such transfer by way of such registration.
